_about: 3 questions per street (what happened · why · think), 3 options each; answer = index of the right option (options are shuffled on screen). evidence = the supporting sentence from the text, for review only — never shown to players. hint = the gentle 'look again' line shown after a wrong answer or bought with coins.

nursery.q: Where was the Velveteen Rabbit on Christmas morning?
options: In the top of the Boy's stocking
Under the Christmas tree
In a box on the table
nursery.evidence: On Christmas morning, when he sat wedged in the top of the Boy's stocking, with a sprig of holly between his paws, the effect was charming.
nursery.hint: Look again at the very first part, on Christmas morning.

nursery.q: Why did the Rabbit start sleeping in the Boy's bed?
options: The Boy couldn't find his china dog, so Nana gave him the Rabbit
The Rabbit was the Boy's newest present
The Skin Horse asked Nana to put him there
nursery.evidence: One evening, when the Boy was going to bed, he couldn't find the china dog that always slept with him.
nursery.hint: Look again at the part where Nana is in a hurry at bedtime.

nursery.q: What does the Skin Horse's talk about Real show?
options: Being loved matters more than how you look
The most expensive toys are the most Real
Becoming Real happens all at once, like being wound up
nursery.evidence: But these things don't matter at all, because once you are Real you can't be ugly, except to people who don't understand.
nursery.hint: Look again at what the Skin Horse says about hair being loved off and getting shabby.

garden.q: Where did the Boy leave the Rabbit when he played in the wood?
options: In a little nest in the bracken
Up on the branch of a tree
In the wheelbarrow by the gate
garden.evidence: he always made the Rabbit a little nest somewhere among the bracken, where he would be quite cosy, for he was a kind-hearted little boy and he liked Bunny to be comfortable.
garden.hint: Look again at the part about the wood near the house, in the long June evenings.

garden.q: Why did the Rabbit keep saying he didn't want to play with the wild rabbits?
options: He didn't want them to see he couldn't hop like them
He was too tired after the Boy's games
He was scared of the ants
garden.evidence: That was a dreadful question, for the Velveteen Rabbit had no hind legs at all!
garden.hint: Look again at the part where the wild rabbit asks if he can hop on his hind legs.

garden.q: The wild rabbit said, "He isn't real!" Why did the little Rabbit still say "I am Real!"?
options: Because the Boy loved him and said he was Real
Because he could jump higher than anything
Because he was furry and brand-new
garden.evidence: "I am Real!" said the little Rabbit. "I am Real! The Boy said so!"
garden.hint: Look again at what the little Rabbit says, just before he nearly begins to cry.

fairy.q: What grew where the little Rabbit's tear fell?
options: A mysterious flower
A raspberry cane
A tiny tree
fairy.evidence: For where the tear had fallen a flower grew out of the ground, a mysterious flower, not at all like any that grew in the garden.
fairy.hint: Look again at the part at the end of the garden, at night, after the tear falls.

fairy.q: Why did the old Bunny have to go away with the old picture-books?
options: The doctor said he was full of germs from the Boy's illness
The Boy didn't love him any more
Nana wanted to give him to another child
fairy.evidence: "That?" said the doctor. "Why, it's a mass of scarlet fever germs!
fairy.hint: Look again at what the doctor says when Nana asks about the old Bunny.

fairy.q: The Fairy said, "You were Real to the Boy… Now you shall be Real to every one." What does this show?
options: The Boy's love had made him Real, and now everyone would see it
He was never Real at all until the Fairy came
Only fairies can make toys Real
fairy.evidence: "You were Real to the Boy," the Fairy said, "because he loved you. Now you shall be Real to every one."
fairy.hint: Look again at what the Fairy says when the Rabbit asks, "Wasn't I Real before?"

vault.q: Who was the only one kind to the Velveteen Rabbit in the nursery at first?
options: The Skin Horse
Timothy, the wooden lion
The model boat
vault.evidence: Between them all the poor little Rabbit was made to feel himself very insignificant and commonplace, and the only person who was kind to him at all was the Skin Horse.
vault.hint: Think back to the very start, in the nursery.

vault.q: Who first said out loud that the Rabbit was REAL?
options: The Boy
Nana
The wild rabbits
vault.evidence: "Give me my Bunny!" he said. "You mustn't say that. He isn't a toy. He's REAL!"
vault.hint: Think about the night the Rabbit was left out on the lawn.

vault.q: What happened to the Rabbit while the Boy loved him so hard?
options: He grew old and shabby, and his whiskers were loved off
He grew shinier and newer every day
He grew clockwork inside him
vault.evidence: He loved him so hard that he loved all his whiskers off, and the pink lining to his ears turned grey, and his brown spots faded.
vault.hint: The Skin Horse said this would happen to anyone who becomes Real.

vault.q: What did the wild rabbits have that the Velveteen Rabbit longed for?
options: Hind legs to hop and dance with
Clockwork keys
Ears lined with pink sateen
vault.evidence: But all the while he was longing to dance, for a funny new tickly feeling ran through him, and he felt he would give anything in the world to be able to jump about like these rabbits did.
vault.hint: Think about the summer evening in the bracken.

vault.q: What does the nursery magic Fairy do for playthings that children have loved?
options: She takes them away and turns them into Real
She mends them so they look new again
She gives them to other children
vault.evidence: When they are old and worn out and the children don't need them any more, then I come and take them away with me and turn them into Real.
vault.hint: Think about what the Fairy says when she first speaks to the Rabbit.

vault.q: In the spring, why did one of the rabbits in the wood look familiar to the Boy?
options: He had spots showing through his fur, like the old Bunny
He was wearing the Boy's scarf
He came when the Boy called his name
vault.evidence: One of them was brown all over, but the other had strange markings under his fur, as though long ago he had been spotted, and the spots still showed through.
vault.hint: Think about the very last part of the story.

vault.q: What does the whole story say makes you Real?
options: Being truly loved for a long, long time
Being expensive and clever
Never getting old or worn out
vault.evidence: When a child loves you for a long, long time, not just to play with, but REALLY loves you, then you become Real.
vault.hint: Think about the Skin Horse — and about the Boy.
